# Remove-ZbxHost

## SYNOPSIS

Removes hosts.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxHost [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A host is a monitored device, server or application: a name, the groups it is in, the interfaces it is polled on, and the items, triggers and templates that monitor it. The Remove-ZbxHost cmdlet deletes the hosts given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with host.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a host by name

```powershell
Remove-ZbxHost -InputObject 'web-02' -Confirm:$false
```

-InputObject takes a name, an id or a host object. ConfirmImpact is High, so PowerShell asks first unless -Confirm:$false is given.

### Example 2: Delete every host a search finds, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-02*' | Remove-ZbxHost -WhatIf
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-02*' | Remove-ZbxHost -Confirm:$false
```

Get-ZbxHost writes host objects; Remove-ZbxHost binds each one. Run it with -WhatIf first to see what would go.
